title: First Council of Nicaea (325)
author: Council of Nicaea I
blurb: The first ecumenical council: the Nicene Creed, the twenty canons, the synodal letter and the decision on the date of Easter, with Percival's historical introduction and excursuses on the word homoousios.

title: First Council of Constantinople (381)
author: Council of Constantinople I
blurb: The second ecumenical council: the Creed of Constantinople (the Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed said at Mass), its seven canons and synodical letter, with the editor's notes on the later addition of the Filioque.

title: Council of Ephesus (431)
author: Council of Ephesus
blurb: The third ecumenical council: extracts from the Acts, Cyril's letters and twelve anathematisms against Nestorius, the letter of Pope Celestine, and the canons. It affirmed Mary as Theotokos, the God-bearer.

title: Council of Chalcedon (451)
author: Council of Chalcedon
blurb: The fourth ecumenical council: extracts from the Acts, the Tome of Leo, the Definition of Faith (one person in two natures) and the thirty canons.

title: Second Council of Constantinople (553)
author: Council of Constantinople II
blurb: The fifth ecumenical council: extracts from the Acts, the Capitula (anathemas on the Three Chapters and Origen), and the decretal letter of Pope Vigilius.

title: Third Council of Constantinople (680–681)
author: Council of Constantinople III
blurb: The sixth ecumenical council: extracts from the Acts, the letter of Pope Agatho, the Definition of Faith (two wills in Christ) and the sentence against the Monothelites, with the editor's excursus on Pope Honorius.

title: Second Council of Nicaea (787)
author: Council of Nicaea II
blurb: The seventh ecumenical council: extracts from the Acts, the Decree on the veneration of holy images and the canons.

title: The Canons and Decrees of the Council of Trent
author: Council of Trent
blurb: All twenty-five sessions of the Council of Trent in English, with the dogmatic chapters and canons (original sin, Scripture, justification, the sacraments, the Mass, purgatory) and the decrees of reformation, followed by Pius IV's bull of confirmation. Machine OCR, not proofread.

title: First Vatican Council: Dei Filius and Pastor Aeternus

Machine OCR, repaired for lost line-end hyphens, not proofread.

title: Ineffabilis Deus: Definition of the Immaculate Conception
